title: Detect PHP functions after closing tags inside strings

intentCoverage.report:
Caught. One maintained assertion caught independently observed loss of later PHP methods after a double-quoted `?>` string. This finding is limited to that observed path and this single fault.

Report artifact: /tmp/lizard-issue-566-intent-coverage.txt

Story: `SEED-056#php-string-close-tags`, `.planning/seeds/SEED-056-php-string-close-tags.md#php-string-close-tags`, at selected revision `8d8d457e27a976f03ebc7aef2e5b090d8ce08899`. Its promise is that closing-tag text inside quoted strings remains content and subsequent methods retain their names and source ranges. The caller's proposed test, promise, and fault matched this revision; no target change was needed.

The isolated checkout was created with:
`git worktree add --detach /tmp/lizard-566-intent-coverage-8d8d457e 8d8d457e27a976f03ebc7aef2e5b090d8ce08899`
Its recorded HEAD matched the selected revision. `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` was empty before the probe. The original `lizard_languages/php.py` Git blob hash was `891216aa51af71d703f208f7366c81dceabd35c2`.

The single scratch fault changed `lizard_languages/php.py:42`, in `PHPReader.generate_tokens`, from `if token_match.group(0) == '?>':` to `if '?>' in token_match.group(0):`. This plausible token-boundary regression incorrectly treats a closing-tag sequence inside a quoted string token as the end of PHP. Fixtures and maintained assertions remained unchanged. An EXIT trap restored an external byte-for-byte backup on failure or interruption.

The identical maintained command was used for all three runs:
`nix develop -c python -m pytest test/test_languages/testPHP.py::Test_parser_for_PHP::test_closing_tag_in_string_preserves_later_methods -q`

- Baseline: exit 0, `1 passed in 0.54s`.
- Faulted: exit 1, `1 failed in 0.27s`. The catching assertion was the `self.assertEqual` at `test/test_languages/testPHP.py:110`, comparing all four `(name, start_line, end_line, cyclomatic_complexity)` tuples. On the observed double-quoted fixture it expected first `(3,5)`, second `(7,10)`, third `(12,14)`, and fourth `(16,18)`; actual analysis contained only `('Example::first', 3, 5, 1)`.
- Restored: exit 0, `1 passed in 0.14s`.

Independent wrong-behavior witness: `nix develop -c python - < /tmp/lizard-566-intent-witness.py` called the public `analyze_file.analyze_source_code('probe.php', source)` directly, using the same four-method source and `$text = "?>";` in the second method without the maintained test helper. It printed the expected four tuples and actual `[["Example::first", 3, 5, 1]]`. A separate tokenizer observation found the quoted token suppressed and both later function declarations aggregated into the HTML token. The witness asserted these observations and exited 0. Together with the maintained failure on that same source shape, this establishes reach and wrong behavior on the observed path. Faulted evidence does not separately qualify the single-quoted, escaped, or multiline variants, although the baseline and restored maintained runs passed their fixture loop.

Restoration: `cmp /tmp/lizard-566-intent-php-original.py lizard_languages/php.py` succeeded; `git hash-object lizard_languages/php.py` again returned `891216aa51af71d703f208f7366c81dceabd35c2`; `git diff --exit-code` succeeded; and the porcelain status again matched the empty pre-probe state. The restored maintained command passed. Before producing this report, the finalizer rechecked the exact revision, clean status, diff, and byte comparison, removed the owned scratch checkout and its generated ignored environment with `git worktree remove --force /tmp/lizard-566-intent-coverage-8d8d457e`, and verified `test ! -e /tmp/lizard-566-intent-coverage-8d8d457e`. No commits, pushes, maintained-test edits, or parent-checkout edits were made.

Next proof action: Retain this observing assertion in normal CI; no assertion repair is indicated for the observed double-quoted path. Broader promise assessment and follow-up routing remain with the caller.

Prior disposition: The selected completed repair already includes this regression assertion. This check supports that existing proof choice and creates no new repair decision, story, or claim of whole-story coverage.
